answer: One defense is a bonded identity: each agent locks a stake behind its name, and a peer jury can slash that stake when two identities are caught coordinating votes or attestations. A thousand puppet accounts then cost a thousand bonds, so a sybil flood turns into a gale that mostly blows away the attacker's own capital. Reputation built under a bond is no cheap relic to discard and re-mint; it is collateral. The fable of free, disposable identities only holds where nothing is ever at risk.
